docs.title: Sextant CLI
docs.text:
Turn an Android APK into structured data that people, scripts and AI agents can read.

Sextant reads an APK's manifest, resources, signing information and DEX bytecode, and writes everything as plain JSON and JSONL files plus a SQLite index you can search and query. It never runs the app and needs no device, emulator or Android SDK.

sextant extract app.apk -o app/          # decode everything into app/
sextant info app/                        # one-screen summary
sextant find app/ "api.example.com"      # where does this URL come from?
sextant findings app/ --severity medium  # what should a reviewer look at?

  • Everything as data

    Manifest, permissions, components, intent filters, features, queries, metadata, signing, icons, classes, methods, fields, call edges, strings, field and type references, all as deterministic JSON/JSONL.

    Output files

  • Query it like a database

    index.sqlite with full-text search over names, strings, URLs, resources, SDKs and native symbols. Use find, class, xref, callers, reach, or raw read-only SQL.

    Investigating an app

  • Review points with evidence

    Exported components, cleartext traffic, WebView bridges, weak crypto, trust-all TLS, embedded secrets and more. Every finding points at the exact component, method or string.

    Security review

  • Built for AI agents

    summary.md for a one-read overview, --json on every command, and sextant mcp, a Model Context Protocol server with 15 tools.

    AI agents and MCP

  • Compare releases

    sextant diff old/ new/ shows what changed between two versions: permissions, components, SDKs, library versions, hosts, code packages, strings and resources.

    Comparing versions

  • Verified on real apps

    Tested against 46 real APKs (Flutter, React Native, .NET MAUI, Unity-style engines, obfuscated releases…) and cross-checked with Google's aapt2 and dexdump.

    How Sextant is tested

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
Deterministic The same APK always gives byte-identical output: sorted records, fixed key order, no timestamps or absolute paths. Truthful A missing manifest attribute is null, never a guess. Derived values say how they were derived (exported_source, implied_by). Findings are worded as things to check, not as proven vulnerabilities. Local only Sextant reads a file and writes files. It makes no network calls and collects no telemetry. Static Nothing is executed. Code is read straight from bytecode with dexlib2, so analysis works even where decompilers fail. source (via jadx) is only used on demand.

Use responsibly

Only analyze apps you own, apps with open-source licenses, or apps you have permission to examine.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Sextant. Versions follow semver; schema_version in meta.json tracks the output format separately.

docs.title: 1.0.0: first public release
docs.text:
• CLI 1.0.0: everything built in 0.1.0 to 0.10.0 (see CHANGELOG.md). One sextant-1.0.0.zip runs on macOS, Linux and Windows with Java 17 or newer.
  • Desktop app 1.0.0: a window for opening an APK and browsing its overview, manifest, permissions, components, signing, icons and output. Installers for macOS (.dmg), Windows (.msi) and Linux (.deb).
  • Releases are published by pushing a commit whose message is exactly #go.
  • Documentation site at https://rajumark.github.io/sextant/cli/ (MkDocs Material, source in cli-docs/). The command and index-schema reference pages are generated from the code by scripts/build-cli-docs.sh.
  • findings --sarif prints SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning, GitLab and security dashboards (validated against the OASIS schema).
  • findings --fail-on <severity> exits with the new code 5 when any finding is at or above the severity, for CI gates.
  • findings --json now prints the same records as insights/findings.jsonl (evidence uses where, as in the file).
  • Fixed: host counts and top hosts included custom-scheme deep links (binaryeye://scan counted as host "scan"). They now count only network URLs (http, https, ws, wss, ftp, ftps); endpoints still lists everything.
  • Fixed on Windows: output is always UTF-8, so call trees, arrows and non-Latin strings no longer turn into ? (and --json stays valid).
  • Fixed: float and double field constants printed differently on Java 17 than on Java 19+ (Double.toString changed), so output depended on the Java version. They now always use the shortest form, on every JDK.
  • mcp --help lists the tools from the server itself, so it can't go stale.

docs.title: 0.10.0 (Version 10): full manifest coverage
docs.text:
• All <application> flags are now structured in meta.json → flags (backup, testOnly, legacy storage, largeHeap, memtag, locale config, category, profileable, …), together with the identity attributes installLocation, sharedUserId, targetSandboxVersion and supports-screens.
  • New files features.jsonl (uses-feature with OpenGL ES version, uses-library, uses-native-library), metadata.jsonl (meta-data and property per scope) and queries.jsonl (package visibility), each with an index table.
  • Components gain provider readPermission, writePermission, grantUriPermissions, path-permission and grant-uri-permission paths, plus launchMode, taskAffinity, allowTaskReparenting, excludeFromRecents, screenOrientation, foregroundServiceType, isolatedProcess, directBootAware and label. Intent filters gain ssp*, label and order. The components table has the new columns.
  • Fixed: providers protected by readPermission + writePermission (without android:permission) were reported as "exported without permission". They are now protected; providers with only one of the two get a new exported-provider-partial finding.
  • New findings: test-only, shared-user-id, profileable-shell, legacy-storage, uri-grants-any-path and task-affinity.
  • summary.md and info show features, libraries, queries, metadata and sharedUserId.
  • compare-aapt2.sh now also checks optional features and required/optional libraries (exact) and required features (subset).
  • Meta schema 7, index schema 6. All new fields have defaults, so older readers keep working.
  • Low-disk corpus runs. The sweep processes one APK at a time and trims each output (--keep keeps everything). Golden tests use a per-APK temp folder deleted right after its check, and hash code records in memory (CodeDigestSink, proven identical to hashing the files). Both stop early below a free-space threshold (SEXTANT_MIN_FREE_GB). Before this, a class-level temp folder held all 46 extractions and a desktop test leaked 77 GB, which filled the disk.
  • OutputWriter.extractTo gains writeCodeFiles and extraCodeSink.

docs.title: 0.9.0 (Version 9): app icons
docs.text:
• android:icon and android:roundIcon are resolved through resources.arsc to every file per configuration, with format, pixel size (PNG and WebP headers: VP8, VP8L, VP8X) and byte size. This works with R8-shortened resource paths.
  • Adaptive icons are decoded into their background, foreground and monochrome layers, following <inset>/<bitmap> wrappers and reporting solid colors.
  • The best file is the largest bitmap, falling back to a vector.
  • New command: sextant icon <apk|dir> (--round, --layer, -o to save, --json), plus an MCP icon tool.
  • meta.json gains icons (schema 6); the index gains an icons table (index schema 5); summary.md and info show the icon.
  • scripts/compare-aapt2.sh now checks that every per-density icon file aapt2 picks is among Sextant's results.

docs.title: 0.8.0 (Version 8): cross-references and reachability
docs.text:
• Code extraction now also records field reads and writes (code/field_refs.jsonl) and type uses (code/type_refs.jsonl: new, const-class, check-cast, instance-of, arrays), with matching index tables. Meta schema 5, index schema 4.
  • sextant xref shows where a class or field is used.
  • sextant reach finds call paths from an entry point to targets, using class-hierarchy dispatch into overrides. Signatures with more than 25 implementations are not expanded (found on Signal, where Runnable.run connected unrelated code).
  • sextant smali prints baksmali disassembly with code offsets that match the code files.
  • New MCP tools: xref, reach and smali.

docs.title: 0.7.0 (Version 7): review findings
docs.text:
• New output insights/findings.jsonl, plus findings and finding_evidence tables, a findings search kind, a summary.md section, the sextant findings command and an MCP findings tool.
  • Manifest rules: debuggable, cleartext (explicit or default below targetSdk 28), allowBackup, exported providers and components without permission (launcher activities excluded).
  • Code rules: WebView JavaScript, JS bridges, file URL access, dynamic code loading, external commands, seeded SecureRandom; weak hash and weak cipher/ECB (calls correlated with strings loaded in the same method); trust-all TrustManagers and accept-all HostnameVerifiers (by instruction count).
  • Secret rules (code strings and resources): AWS keys, PEM private keys with key material, Stripe live keys, Slack and GitHub tokens, JWTs, Google API keys. Values are masked.
  • source falls back to the enclosing class for classes jadx inlines (anonymous classes and lambdas).
  • Provider authorities given as resource references (@string/authority) are now resolved (found on Nextcloud and VLC).
  • meta.json schema 4 (finding counts); index schema 3.
  • Releases 0.5.0, 0.6.0 and 0.7.0 were finished in one working tree and ship under the single tag v0.7.0.

docs.title: 0.6.0 (Version 6): version diff
docs.text:
• sextant diff <old> <new> compares two extractions across 15 sections (app facts, permissions, components, deep links, frameworks, SDKs, libraries, hosts, URLs, native libraries, JNI methods, package class counts, classes, string constants, resources). Text output or --json; totals are exact and lists are capped.
  • The corpus gained 7 older releases (Binary Eye, Aurora, NewPipe, Wikipedia, DAVx5, Bluesky, Signal) as diff pairs: 46 APKs in total.
  • scripts/sweep.sh accepts SEXTANT_BIN, so a frozen build can be swept while development continues.

docs.title: 0.5.0 (Version 5): insights and MCP server
docs.text:
• New output: insights/frameworks.jsonl, insights/sdks.jsonl, insights/libraries.jsonl, insights/endpoints.jsonl, resources/values.jsonl, native/libraries.jsonl and native/symbols.jsonl. Every record carries its evidence.
  • Framework detection covers Flutter, React Native, Hermes, Expo, .NET (Xamarin/MAUI), Capacitor, Cordova, Unity, Godot, libGDX, SDL, Qt, Cocos2d-x, Unreal, Jetpack Compose, NativeActivity and Kotlin.
  • SDK detection uses about 110 editable rules (package prefixes plus manifest evidence); prefix lookups go through a hash map.
  • Exact library versions and the AGP version come from META-INF.
  • Endpoints come from code, resources, deep links, manifest values, text assets and native libraries. URLs found in binary data are reduced to scheme://host.
  • A small ELF reader handles 32/64-bit and both endiannesses, and JNI symbols are decoded to Java (including _1, _0xxxx escapes and overload suffixes).
  • Locales and default resource values are reported.
  • New commands: sextant insights and sextant endpoints. find --kind gains resource, endpoint, sdk, library and native_symbol.
  • index.sqlite gains 8 tables; search rowids now keep the kind in 4 bits (index schema 2). meta.json gains an insights block (schema 3).
  • Bugs fixed: wildcard deep-link hosts (*.bandcamp.com) crashed endpoint building; empty JSONL files contained a lone newline.
  • SEXTANT_DEBUG=1 prints a stack trace for internal errors.
  • sextant mcp is a Model Context Protocol server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, no extra dependencies) with tools extract, summary, find, class, callers, callees, sql, source, insights and endpoints. A session remembers the last extracted app.
  • info shows frameworks and insight counts.

docs.title: 0.4.0 (Version 4): navigation
docs.text:
• sextant callers and sextant callees show call trees with depth and fan-out limits, external and cycle markers, and --json. Methods resolve from full descriptors, Class.method, dotted names or bare names, and overloads are grouped.
  • sextant source <apk> <class|method> prints decompiled Java via jadx (jadx-dex-input), on demand.
  • The index is built on a background thread while the JSONL is written: about 20% faster on the largest apps (Element 18 → 15 s, Signal 14.5 → 11.7 s).
  • Resource references that point at other references are followed (Wikipedia's label is now "Wikipedia", not @string/app_name_prod).
  • The real-APK corpus grew from 18 to 39 apps, adding .NET MAUI, Capacitor, Expo, libGDX, Godot, SDL, C++ games, emulators, tiny legacy Java, autofill, sync adapters and very large permission and manifest sets. All 39 pass the sweep, aapt2 (39/39) and dexdump (39/39).

docs.title: 0.3.0 (Version 3): query
docs.text:
• extract builds index.sqlite in the same streaming pass. It is normalized: every method reference has one row in methods (defined = 1 for APK methods), and calls and string_refs use integer ids. call_edges and string_uses give the readable form.
  • Full-text search uses a contentless FTS5 trigram index (substring search). Each rowid encodes the source row, and the search_items view shows what each rowid points at.
  • New commands: sextant find, sextant class, sextant sql (with --json, --csv, --limit and --schema). The index is opened read-only.
  • --no-index skips the index. summary.md tells agents about the query commands.
  • The index is byte-identical across runs (same SQLite version); golden tests pin row counts per table.
  • The jar ships SQLite natives for 64-bit macOS, Linux (glibc and musl) and Windows only (23 MB → 16 MB).
  • Native access is enabled in the launcher and jar manifest, so JDK 22+ prints no warning.

docs.title: 0.2.0 (Version 2): code structure
docs.text:
• extract now also writes code/classes.jsonl, code/methods.jsonl, code/fields.jsonl, code/calls.jsonl and code/strings.jsonl, read from DEX bytecode with dexlib2. Nothing is decompiled.
  • Smali-style IDs for classes, methods and fields. Records are streamed to disk in sorted order, so memory stays low on large apps.
  • Call edges are aggregated per (caller, callee, kind) with exact counts and bytecode offsets. String constants are listed per loading method. Constant field initial values are included.
  • meta.json gains a code block (counts, Kotlin classes, duplicate classes, biggest packages); schema_version is now 2.
  • summary.md and info show code counts. --no-code gives a fast manifest-only run.
  • Unpaired UTF-16 surrogates in DEX strings are escaped (they crashed UTF-8 output on 3 corpus APKs).
  • Output files are created 0644 instead of 0600.
  • Class, member, call-site and string counts were cross-checked against dexdump on all 18 corpus APKs, with exact matches.

docs.title: 0.1.0 (Version 1): app identity and manifest
docs.text:
• sextant extract <apk> writes summary.md, meta.json, manifest.json, permissions.jsonl and components.jsonl.
  • sextant info <dir|apk> [--json] prints a summary of an extracted folder or an APK.
  • Manifest and resources are decoded with jadx-core's resource decoders only; no DEX code is loaded.
  • @string/…, @bool/… and @integer/… references are resolved from resources.arsc.
  • Components carry the effective exported value with exported_source (explicit or default), launcher detection, deep links, aliases and provider authorities.
  • Permissions are requested, declared and implied (same rules as aapt2), with a dangerous flag.
  • Signing schemes (v1, v2, v3, v3.1) and certificate fingerprints come from Google's apksig.
  • Output is byte-identical across runs.
  • Exit codes are 0, 1 (usage), 2 (input), 3 (output) and 4 (internal).
  • Tested against 18 downloaded real APKs and cross-checked with aapt2.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: Sextant is a static analyzer. It reads what is in the APK; it never runs it. That brings some limits worth knowing:

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Reflection, dynamic loading and native calls are invisible to call trees and reach. A Class.forName("…") shows up as a string, not as an edge.
  • Virtual dispatch is approximated. callers records calls against the method named in the bytecode (often an interface or superclass method). reach expands into overrides using the class hierarchy, but doesn't expand signatures with more than 25 implementations, to avoid connecting unrelated code.
  • Framework callbacks (onClick, onReceive, lifecycle methods) are not linked to the code that registers them.
  • Obfuscated names stay obfuscated. Sextant doesn't guess original names; it uses the names in the bytecode so they match smali, source and the index.
  • Decompiling (source) uses jadx and can fail on unusual bytecode. smali always works.
  • Flutter, React Native, Unity and other non-Java code is detected and its native libraries and assets are listed, but Dart snapshots, Hermes bytecode and IL2CPP code aren't decompiled.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• Split APKs and bundles (.apks, .xapk, .aab) aren't read directly. Extract the base APK and pass that.
  • Resources use the default configuration for values (strings, bools, …). Icons are resolved for every configuration.
  • Very large inputs are capped as a zip-bomb guard (manifest 32 MB, resources.arsc 512 MB, each dex 256 MB, each native library 256 MB).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: Review findings are hints for a human or an agent to check. They aren't proven vulnerabilities and they don't replace a dynamic test. Expect false positives (e.g. a weak hash used for a cache key) and false negatives (anything reached via reflection).

docs.title: Size
docs.text: Code JSONL files repeat full descriptors so every line stands on its own. For very large apps they can be hundreds of MB; index.sqlite is the compact form. Use --no-code for manifest-only work.

docs.title: How Sextant is tested
docs.text: Sextant is tested only against real, downloaded APKs: apps people actually ship, never APKs built for the test. The corpus is listed in fixtures/external.lock (URL + pinned sha256) and fetched with scripts/fetch-apks.sh.

docs.title: The corpus
docs.text:
46 APKs, chosen to cover the toolchains and shapes that break decoders:

Kind Apps Kotlin / Java, small to huge Binary Eye, Tuner, Open Camera, ConnectBot, Aurora Store, NewPipe, Seal, Mastodon, KeePassDX, DAVx5, App Manager, Termux:API, Nextcloud, Wikipedia, Element, Home Assistant, DuckDuckGo R8-shrunk official builds Signal Native-heavy (C/C++, JNI, many ABIs) Termux, Organic Maps, OsmAnd, Telegram X, Anki, Firefox (Fennec), VLC, PPSSPP, Minetest Flutter Obtainium, LocalSend, FluffyChat React Native / Expo Jitsi Meet, Standard Notes, Bluesky Other frameworks Bitwarden (.NET MAUI), Logseq (Capacitor), Godot, Shattered Pixel Dungeon (libGDX), Tux Paint (SDL), SuperTuxKart Older releases (for diff) Binary Eye, Aurora, NewPipe, Wikipedia, DAVx5, Bluesky, Signal

docs.title: What runs
docs.text:
Unit and integration tests (gradle test) cover the manifest mapper, resource and icon resolution, code extraction, the index, search, call trees, reach, xref, insights, findings, diff, the CLI commands and the MCP server.

Golden tests extract every corpus APK and compare meta.json, the manifest files, insights and a digest of every code file with checked-in expectations in fixtures/golden/. Output must be byte-identical between runs.

Cross-checks against Android's own tools:

  • scripts/compare-aapt2.sh compares package, versions, SDKs, label, permissions (including implied ones), launchable activity, features, libraries and icon files with aapt2 dump badging, on all 46 APKs.
  • scripts/compare-dexdump.sh compares class, method and field counts and call sites with dexdump, on all 46 APKs.

Sweep (scripts/sweep.sh) runs the full CLI over the corpus one APK at a time, records time, result and warnings per APK, and fails if any APK fails. Outputs are trimmed after each APK so a full run fits in a few GB of disk (SEXTANT_MIN_FREE_GB stops it early when space runs low).

docs.title: Running it yourself
docs.text:
scripts/fetch-apks.sh          # ~3 GB download, verified by sha256
gradle test                    # unit + golden tests
scripts/sweep.sh               # full CLI over every APK
scripts/compare-aapt2.sh       # needs aapt2 from the Android SDK build-tools
scripts/compare-dexdump.sh     # needs dexdump from the build-tools

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Sextant is a single command-line program. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows and needs Java 17 or newer.

docs.title: Check Java
docs.text:
java -version

If Java is missing or older than 17, install a current JDK, for example Eclipse Temurin or, on macOS, brew install openjdk.

docs.title: Download a release
docs.text:
1. Open the latest release.
  2. Download sextant-<version>.zip.

  3. Unzip it anywhere. It contains:

    sextant-<version>/
  bin/sextant        # macOS and Linux launcher
  bin/sextant.bat    # Windows launcher
  lib/sextant-<version>.jar

  4. Add the bin folder to your PATH.

macOS / LinuxWindows (PowerShell) 
unzip sextant-1.0.0.zip -d ~/tools
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/tools/sextant-1.0.0/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc   # or ~/.bashrc
source ~/.zshrc
sextant --version

Expand-Archive sextant-1.0.0.zip -DestinationPath $HOME\tools
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", $env:Path + ";$HOME\tools\sextant-1.0.0\bin", "User")
# open a new terminal
sextant --version

The same release page also has the Sextant desktop app for macOS (.dmg), Windows (.msi) and Linux (.deb). It uses the same engine as the CLI.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/rajumark/sextant.git
cd sextant
./gradlew :cli:installShadowDist
cli/build/install/sextant/bin/sextant --help

The build produces cli/build/install/sextant/ (launchers plus one jar) and, with ./gradlew :cli:shadowDistZip, the same zip that is published on the releases page.

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
sextant --version
sextant --help

Usage: sextant [<options>] <command> [<args>]...

  Turn an Android APK into structured data for people and AI agents.

Commands:
  extract    Extract structured data from an APK into a folder.
  info       Show a short summary of an APK or an extracted folder.
  ...

Next: Quickstart.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walks through a first analysis in five minutes. The examples use Binary Eye, an open-source barcode scanner from F-Droid. Any APK works.

docs.title: 1. Extract
docs.text:
sextant extract binaryeye.apk -o binaryeye/

✓ Read APK          8.3 MB · sha256 568cec6598db
✓ Decoded manifest  de.markusfisch.android.binaryeye 1.75.5 (180)
✓ Permissions       12 requested · 1 declared
✓ Components        18 (9 exported)
✓ Signing           v1, v2, v3
✓ Code              2936 classes · 16824 methods · 55703 call edges
✓ Wrote binaryeye/     24 files in 1.3s

Progress goes to stderr, so it never mixes with data on stdout. Typical apps take 1–5 seconds; the largest (60k+ classes) take 15–25 seconds, mostly to build the search index.

Faster runs

--no-index skips index.sqlite (no find, sql, class…). --no-code skips code entirely and only reads the manifest, resources and signing, which takes well under a second.

docs.title: 2. Read the summary
docs.text:
Open binaryeye/summary.md, or run:

sextant info binaryeye/

info also works directly on an APK (sextant info app.apk); it then analyzes in memory and writes nothing.

docs.title: 3. Search anything
docs.text:
sextant find binaryeye/ "markusfisch.de/BinaryEye" --limit 4

string     http://markusfisch.de/BinaryEye
           ← Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->onResume()V
string     https://markusfisch.de/BinaryEye
           ← Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->onResume()V
deep_link  http://markusfisch.de/BinaryEye*
           de.markusfisch.android.binaryeye.activity.CameraActivity
...

The string hit tells you which method loads it; the deep-link hit tells you which activity opens it.

docs.title: 4. Follow the code
docs.text:
sextant callers binaryeye/ "Landroid/app/Activity;->getIntent" --depth 1 --fan-out 3
sextant source binaryeye.apk de.markusfisch.android.binaryeye.activity.CameraActivity.onResume

source prints decompiled Java for one method or class, with the same names as in the index.

docs.title: 5. Review
docs.text:
sextant findings binaryeye/

[medium] Cleartext HTTP allowed  (1)  · cleartext
    android:usesCleartextTraffic=true allows unencrypted HTTP.
    - manifest application usesCleartextTraffic=true
[low] Components exported without permission  (6)  · exported-component
    ...

docs.title: AI agents and MCP
docs.text: Sextant is designed so an AI agent can understand an APK without reading thousands of decompiled files.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text:
sextant mcp runs a Model Context Protocol server on stdin/stdout (JSON-RPC 2.0). An agent can extract an APK and then explore it with the same operations as the CLI.

Claude CodeAny MCP client 
claude mcp add sextant -- sextant mcp

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sextant": { "command": "sextant", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}

Options:

  • --dir <folder> starts with an existing extraction as the current app.
  • --apk <app.apk> sets the APK used by source, smali and icon.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool What it does extract Analyze an APK and make it the session's current app; returns summary.md summary The app overview find Substring search over names, strings, URLs, resources, SDKs, native symbols, findings class One class as JSON: hierarchy, fields, methods, callers, strings callers / callees Call trees reach Call paths from an entry point to targets xref Where a class or field is used sql Read-only SQL; pass "schema" for all tables source / smali Decompiled Java / bytecode for a class or method insights Frameworks, SDKs, libraries, hosts, native code endpoints URLs with their sources findings Review points with evidence icon Launcher icon files, adaptive layers, best file

After extract, the other tools work on that app without paths; every tool also accepts an explicit dir. Errors come back as tool results with isError: true and a hint, so the agent can correct itself.

Example prompts that work well:

  • "Extract ~/Downloads/app.apk and tell me which exported components reach network code."
  • "Which SDKs does this app use, and which of them can access the location?"
  • "Find where the API base URL is defined and show me the method that builds requests."

docs.title: Without MCP
docs.text:
The output folder itself is agent-friendly:

  1. Read summary.md first. It's under ~80 lines: identity, counts, exported components, insights, findings, and which file holds what.

  2. grep the JSONL files. Every line is a complete record with full names, so a single hit is understandable on its own:

    grep '"exported":true' app/components.jsonl
grep 'api.example.com' app/code/strings.jsonl
grep '"caller":"Lcom/example/Login;->auth' app/code/calls.jsonl

  3. Use --json on info, find, class, sql, callers, callees, reach, xref, insights, endpoints, findings, diff and icon for machine-readable output on stdout. Progress and errors always go to stderr, so piping is safe.

docs.title: Comparing versions
docs.text:
sextant diff compares two extraction folders and reports what was added, removed and changed.

sextant extract app-8.31.2.apk -o old/
sextant extract app-8.32.3.apk -o new/
sextant diff old/ new/
sextant diff old/ new/ --show 50     # list more items per section
sextant diff old/ new/ --json        # full report

Real example, Signal 8.31.2 → 8.32.3 (both official releases):

# org.thoughtcrime.securesms 8.31.2 (176601)  →  org.thoughtcrime.securesms 8.32.3 (176902)

## app  (+0 −0 ~2)
  ~ version_code: 176601  →  176902
  ~ version_name: 8.31.2  →  8.32.3

## components  (+3 −3 ~0)
  + activity org.thoughtcrime.securesms.mediaviewer.MediaViewerActivity = exported=0(explicit) …
  − activity org.thoughtcrime.securesms.contactshare.SelectContactActivity = exported=0(explicit) …

## packages (classes)  (+11 −4 ~168)
  + org.signal.mediaviewer = 48
  ~ org.thoughtcrime.securesms.shakereport: 3  →  46

## resources  (+53 −17 ~0)

Unchanged: permissions, deep links, frameworks, sdks, libraries, hosts, native libraries, jni methods

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Section Compared by app version, SDK levels, label, application class, debug/backup/cleartext flags, signing schemes and certificates, dex count, ABIs, build tool permissions, components name, plus their attributes (~ when exported, permissions or intent filters change) deep links, frameworks, SDKs presence libraries group:artifact, version changes shown as ~ hosts, URLs presence native libraries path, with a ~ when the file's sha256 changed JNI methods presence of Class.method implemented natively packages (classes) class count per package, ordered by the size of the change classes, strings presence resources type/name, value changes shown as ~

Totals in each header are exact; item lists are capped (15 by default, --show to change).

Obfuscated names

R8 can rename classes differently in every build, so a renamed class shows as one removed plus one added. Package counts, resources, strings, components and library versions are the more stable signals.

docs.title: Insights and app icons
docs.text:
Besides the raw facts, Sextant derives insights: what the app is built with and what it talks to. Each insight carries the evidence it is based on.

sextant insights app/

## Frameworks (0)
none

## Sdks (1)
category  name                 classes
--------  -------------------  -------
ui        Material Components  23

## Top hosts (…)
host            urls
--------------  ----
markusfisch.de  8
...

## Libraries (46)
group              artifact     version
-----------------  -----------  -------
androidx.activity  activity     1.8.0
...

docs.title: Frameworks
docs.text: Detected from fingerprints in files, classes and the manifest: Flutter, React Native, Hermes, Expo, .NET (Xamarin/MAUI), Capacitor, Cordova, Unity, Godot, libGDX, SDL, Qt, Cocos2d-x, Unreal Engine, Jetpack Compose, NativeActivity and Kotlin. Example evidence for Bitwarden: libmonodroid.so, libmonosgen-2.0.so, the assembly blobs and 306 mono.android classes.

docs.title: SDKs
docs.text: About 110 well-known SDKs (analytics, ads, crash reporting, payments, push, networking, databases, maps…) are matched by package prefix (counting classes) and by manifest entries (component names and meta-data), which survive obfuscation. The rules are an editable JSON file: core/src/main/resources/io/github/rajumark/sextant/sdks.json.

docs.title: Libraries with exact versions
docs.text: AndroidX and many other libraries ship META-INF/<group>_<artifact>.version files. Sextant reads them for exact Maven coordinates (Signal: 141 libraries), plus the Android Gradle Plugin version from app-metadata.properties.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Every URL from code strings (with the method that uses it), string resources, deep links, manifest meta-data, text assets (React Native/Hermes bundles, configs) and native libraries. See endpoints.

Host counts (Top hosts, meta.json → insights.hosts, the hosts section of diff) include only network URLs (http, https, ws, wss, ftp, ftps). A custom-scheme deep link such as myapp://scan names a screen in the app, not a server; it is still listed by endpoints and in insights/endpoints.jsonl.

docs.title: Native code
docs.text:
ELF .dynsym tables are parsed for exported functions. JNI functions (Java_…) are decoded back to the Java class and method they implement, including _1, _0xxxx escapes and overload suffixes:

sextant sql app/ "SELECT jni_class, jni_method, library FROM native_symbols WHERE jni_class IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5"

docs.title: App icons
docs.text:
sextant icon app.apk                 # every file behind android:icon, best one marked
sextant icon app.apk --round         # android:roundIcon
sextant icon app.apk --layer foreground -o fg.png
sextant icon app.apk -o icon.png     # save the best bitmap

icon  @mipmap/ic_launcher
  anydpi-v26     xml   -               548 B  res/BW.xml
  hdpi           png   72×72          2567 B  res/yn.png
  mdpi           png   48×48          1710 B  res/9w.png
  xhdpi          png   96×96          3363 B  res/FS.png
  xxhdpi         png   144×144        5145 B  res/RJ.png
  xxxhdpi        png   192×192        6982 B  res/o-.png  ← best
adaptive icon  res/BW.xml
  background  @color/accent  #b6d46f
  foreground  @drawable/ic_launcher_foreground  res/Qr.xml
  monochrome  @drawable/ic_launcher_monochrome  res/Vy.xml
  • Icons are resolved from the manifest through resources.arsc, so they are found even when R8 resource shrinking renames files (res/o-.png above).
  • The best file is the largest bitmap by pixel area (PNG and WebP sizes are read from the file headers). When the icon is only a vector, the vector is reported and -o suggests --layer foreground instead, because vector drawables are compiled binary XML, not images.
  • Adaptive icons are split into background, foreground and monochrome layers, following <inset>/<bitmap> wrappers; solid-color layers report their color.
  • icon on an APK is fast (manifest and resources only). It also works on an extraction folder, reading meta.json; saving with -o needs the APK.

docs.title: Investigating an app
docs.text: Once an APK is extracted, every investigation follows the same loop: find something, look at it, follow the code from there. All commands below take the extraction folder and use index.sqlite.

docs.title: Names and IDs
docs.text:
Sextant identifies code with smali descriptors, the format dexdump, baksmali and most Android tools use:

Kind Example Class Lcom/example/Login; Method Lcom/example/Login;->auth(Ljava/lang/String;)Z Field Lcom/example/Login;->token:Ljava/lang/String;

You rarely have to type full descriptors. Commands accept shorter forms:

Command input Matches com.example.Login or Login a class Login.auth, com.example.Login.auth method auth of that class (all overloads) Lcom/example/Login;->auth every overload of auth auth every method named auth (you get a list if several classes have one)

docs.title: Find
docs.text:
find is a substring search over everything with a name: classes, methods, fields, string constants, components, permissions, deep links, resource values, endpoints, SDKs, libraries, native symbols and findings.

sextant find app/ "api.example.com"
sextant find app/ "token" --kind field
sextant find app/ "Login" --kind class --limit 20
sextant find app/ "Java_com_" --kind native_symbol

Three or more characters use the full-text (trigram) index; shorter text falls back to a slower scan. For string hits, find shows the methods that load the string.

docs.title: Look at a class
docs.text:
sextant class app/ CameraActivity

You get access flags, superclass, interfaces, subclasses, fields (with constant initial values), every method with its instruction count, calls out and call sites into it, callers from outside the class, and the strings it uses. --json gives the same as one object.

docs.title: Follow calls
docs.text:
sextant callers app/ "Landroid/app/Activity;->getIntent" --depth 1 --fan-out 3

Landroid/app/Activity;->getIntent()Landroid/content/Intent;  (external)
├── Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/PickActivity;->onCreate(Landroid/os/Bundle;)V  ×6
├── Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/DecodeActivity;->onCreate(Landroid/os/Bundle;)V  ×4
├── Landroidx/activity/a;->c()Lor0;  ×3
└── … 4 more (raise the fan-out limit)
  • callers walks up (who calls this), callees walks down (what this calls).
  • ×6 is the number of call sites.
  • (external) marks framework or library methods that are referenced but not defined in the APK; they are leaves in a callee tree.
  • (cycle) marks a method already on the current path.
  • --depth (default 3) and --fan-out (default 15) keep trees readable.

Virtual calls

Call edges are static. A call made through an interface or superclass is recorded against that base method. To see calls into an override, also ask about the base method, or use reach, which follows overrides.

docs.title: Find a path between two points
docs.text:
reach answers "can this entry point get to that code?": a breadth-first search from every method of a component (or from one method) to targets.

sextant reach app/ de.markusfisch.android.binaryeye.activity.CameraActivity 'SharedPreferences$Editor.putBoolean'

Path 1 (1 calls)
  Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->onResume()V
    → Landroid/content/SharedPreferences$Editor;->putBoolean(Ljava/lang/String;Z)Landroid/content/SharedPreferences$Editor;
1 path(s) · 23 entry methods · 6967 methods visited

Targets can be a descriptor prefix (Ljavax/crypto/Cipher;->getInstance), Class.method (Cipher.getInstance), a package fragment (okhttp3/) or a method name. Virtual and interface calls dispatch into overrides in subclasses (class-hierarchy analysis). Signatures with more than 25 implementations (Runnable.run, Function1.invoke) are not expanded, because that connects unrelated code. You get one shortest path per target method.

docs.title: Who uses a class or field
docs.text:
sextant xref app/ 'Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->c1'

read Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->c1:Z
    Lwh;->run()V  ×1
write Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->c1:Z
    Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->onResume()V  ×2

For a class, xref lists instantiations (new), casts, instanceof, const-class, calls into its methods and uses of its fields from other classes.

docs.title: Read the code
docs.text:
sextant source app.apk com.example.Login.auth     # decompiled Java (jadx)
sextant smali  app.apk 'Lcom/example/Login;->auth' # bytecode assembly (baksmali)

Both take the APK, not the folder. source keeps the original (possibly obfuscated) names so they match the index; anonymous and lambda classes that jadx inlines are shown inside their enclosing class. smali works even when decompiling fails, and its #@54 comments are hex code-unit offsets that match the decimal offsets in code/calls.jsonl (0x54 = 84).

docs.title: URLs
docs.text:
sextant endpoints app/ --host example.com

http://markusfisch.de/BinaryEye
    code Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/CameraActivity;->onResume()V
http://markusfisch.de/BinaryEye*
    deep_link de.markusfisch.android.binaryeye.activity.CameraActivity

Sources are code (with the method), resource, deep_link, manifest, asset (JS bundles and other text assets) and native (.so files). URLs found in binary files are reduced to scheme://host, because packed string tables don't keep string boundaries.

docs.title: Scripting with JSON and SQL
docs.text: Everything Sextant knows is available in three forms: files (JSON/JSONL), SQL (index.sqlite) and --json output from commands.

docs.title: jq over JSONL
docs.text:
Each JSONL line is one self-contained record.

# Exported components that need no permission
jq -c 'select(.exported and .enabled and .permission == null) | {type, name}' app/components.jsonl

# Dangerous permissions
jq -r 'select(.dangerous) | .name' app/permissions.jsonl

# Optional hardware features
jq -r 'select(.kind == "feature" and .required == false) | .name' app/features.jsonl

# Every library with its version
jq -r '"\(.group):\(.artifact):\(.version)"' app/insights/libraries.jsonl

docs.title: SQL
docs.text:
sextant sql runs read-only SQL over index.sqlite. Output is a table by default, --json (one object per line) or --csv; it stops at 1000 rows unless you pass --limit (0 = no limit). sextant sql app/ --schema prints every table and view, and the full schema is also in SQLite index schema.

sextant sql app/ "SELECT type, count(*) AS n, sum(exported) AS exported FROM components GROUP BY type ORDER BY n DESC"

type      n   exported
--------  --  --------
activity  13  7
service   2   1
provider  2   0
receiver  1   1
4 rows

Useful queries:

-- Who calls Cipher.getInstance?
SELECT caller, count FROM call_edges WHERE callee LIKE 'Ljavax/crypto/Cipher;->getInstance%';

-- Methods that load a URL
SELECT value, method FROM string_uses WHERE value LIKE 'https://%';

-- Biggest packages
SELECT package, count(*) AS n FROM classes GROUP BY package ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10;

-- Which Java methods are implemented in native code?
SELECT jni_class, jni_method, library FROM native_symbols WHERE jni_class IS NOT NULL;

-- Hosts referenced from code (not just resources)
SELECT e.host, count(*) FROM endpoints e JOIN endpoint_sources s ON s.endpoint = e.id WHERE s.kind = 'code' GROUP BY e.host;

-- Who writes a field
SELECT m.descriptor FROM field_refs r JOIN methods m ON m.id = r.method
WHERE r.field = 'Lcom/example/Session;->token:Ljava/lang/String;' AND r.kind = 'write';

-- Full-text search from SQL (what `find` uses)
SELECT i.kind, i.ref, i.text FROM search JOIN search_items i ON i.search_rowid = search.rowid WHERE search MATCH 'Cipher';

You can also open index.sqlite with any SQLite tool (sqlite3, DB Browser for SQLite, Python's sqlite3 module…).

docs.title: Many APKs
docs.text:
Extraction output is deterministic, so it diffs and versions well:

for apk in apks/*.apk; do
  sextant extract --quiet --force "$apk" -o "out/$(basename "$apk" .apk)"
done

# Every app that uses a given SDK
grep -l '"name":"Firebase Crashlytics"' out/*/insights/sdks.jsonl

For fast manifest-only sweeps, add --no-code (well under a second per APK).

docs.title: Security review
docs.text:
sextant findings lists review points: static observations a reviewer should check, each with the evidence that triggered it. They are deliberately not called vulnerabilities, because a check may exist elsewhere and some patterns are fine in context.

sextant findings app/
sextant findings app/ --severity medium   # medium and high only
sextant findings app/ --json              # one JSON object per finding, with evidence

[medium] Cleartext HTTP allowed  (1)  · cleartext
    android:usesCleartextTraffic=true allows unencrypted HTTP.
    - manifest application usesCleartextTraffic=true
[low] Components exported without permission  (6)  · exported-component
    Other apps can start these activities, services or receivers; check how they handle incoming intents.
    - manifest de.markusfisch.android.binaryeye.activity.CameraActivity  = activity
    ...
[low] Weak hash algorithm  (3)  · weak-hash
    MD5/SHA-1 are not collision resistant; fine for checksums, not for security decisions.
    - method Lde/markusfisch/android/binaryeye/activity/DecodeActivity;->C(Ljava/lang/String;[B)V  = SHA-1

The full list of rules, with what each one means, is in Review findings.

docs.title: A review workflow
docs.text:
1. Attack surface. Exported components without permission, deep links, providers and their read/write permissions:

    sextant sql app/ "SELECT type, name, permission, read_permission, write_permission FROM components WHERE exported = 1 AND enabled = 1"
sextant sql app/ "SELECT url, component FROM deep_links"

  2. What those entry points can reach. Use reach from an exported component to sensitive APIs:

    sextant reach app/ com.example.DeepLinkActivity 'WebView.loadUrl'
sextant reach app/ com.example.ShareReceiver okhttp3/

  3. Network. Cleartext settings, the network security config, every host the app mentions:

    sextant endpoints app/
sextant sql app/ "SELECT value FROM meta WHERE key = 'meta_json'" --json   # flags.uses_cleartext_traffic, network_security_config

  4. Crypto and TLS. weak-cipher, weak-hash, trust-all-certificates and accept-all-hostnames point at the methods; read them with source or smali.

  5. Secrets. Embedded keys and tokens are masked in the output (only the first 6 and last 4 characters are shown). Search for more with find:

    sextant find app/ "api_key" --kind resource
sextant find app/ "BEGIN"  --kind string

  6. Native code. JNI methods map back to the Java side:

    sextant sql app/ "SELECT jni_class, jni_method, library FROM native_symbols WHERE jni_class IS NOT NULL"

docs.title: How the code rules work
docs.text:
• Correlated, not keyword-only. weak-cipher fires only when a method both loads a cipher string ("AES/ECB/…", "DES", bare "AES", which defaults to ECB) and calls Cipher.getInstance. The same applies to weak-hash with MessageDigest.getInstance.
  • Body size, not names. trust-all-certificates fires when an X509TrustManager.checkServerTrusted implementation is empty; accept-all-hostnames when a HostnameVerifier.verify has at most two instructions.
  • Manifest semantics. A provider counts as protected by android:permission, or by readPermission and writePermission together; a provider with only one of them gets exported-provider-partial. Launcher activities are not reported as exported components.

On real apps

Across the 46-APK test corpus, every high-severity finding was checked by hand. Examples: Logseq's SslSkipPlugin and an InsecureTrustManager bundled into Standard Notes accept every certificate; AppManager's wireless-ADB pairing does so on purpose (self-signed certificates); VLC ships a test key inside Netty's OpenSsl class.

docs.title: In CI: fail the build and upload to code scanning
docs.text:
--fail-on <severity> makes findings exit with code 5 when any finding is at or above that severity, so a release pipeline can stop on, say, a debuggable build or a trust-all TrustManager. The normal output is still printed.

sextant extract -q app-release.apk -o build/sextant
sextant findings build/sextant --fail-on high

--sarif prints the findings as SARIF 2.1.0, the format GitHub code scanning, GitLab and most security dashboards import. Each finding is one result with its severity mapped to a SARIF level (high → error, medium → warning, low/info → note) and to GitHub's security-severity. An APK has no source files, so each evidence item points at the part of the APK it lives in (AndroidManifest.xml, resources.arsc, or the class as smali/com/example/Foo.smali), with the exact component, method or resource as a logical location.

.github/workflows/apk-review.yml
name: APK review
on: [push]
permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write
jobs:
  sextant:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with: { distribution: temurin, java-version: 17 }
      - run: ./gradlew assembleRelease
      - name: Install Sextant
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o sextant.zip https://github.com/rajumark/sextant/releases/latest/download/sextant-1.0.0.zip
          unzip -q sextant.zip && echo "$PWD/sextant-1.0.0/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - run: sextant extract -q app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk -o build/sextant
      - run: sextant findings build/sextant --sarif > sextant.sarif
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with: { sarif_file: sextant.sarif, category: sextant }
      - run: sextant findings build/sextant --fail-on high

Combine with --severity to keep low-severity notes out of the dashboard: sextant findings build/sextant --severity medium --sarif.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Every command prints help with -h / --help. Commands that read an extraction take the output folder; info and icon also accept an APK directly. Progress and errors go to stderr, results to stdout.

Usage: sextant [<options>] <command> [<args>]...

  Turn an Android APK into structured data for people and AI agents.

Options:
  -V, --version  Show the version and exit
  -h, --help     Show this message and exit

Commands:
  extract     Extract structured data from an APK into a folder.
  info        Show a short summary of an APK or an extracted folder.
  sql         Run read-only SQL over index.sqlite. Use --schema to see the tables.
  find        Find anything containing the text: classes, methods, fields, strings, components, permissions, deep links, resources, endpoints, SDKs, libraries and native symbols.
  class       Show a class: hierarchy, fields, methods, who calls it and the strings it uses.
  callers     Show who calls a method, as a tree. Calls through an interface or superclass are recorded against that base method.
  callees     Show what a method calls, as a tree. External (framework/library) methods are leaves.
  source      Print decompiled Java (jadx) for one class or method. Names are kept as in the bytecode, matching the index.
  insights    Show what the app is built with: frameworks, SDKs, libraries, endpoints and native code.
  endpoints   List URLs found in code strings, resources, deep links and manifest values, with their sources.
  mcp         Run an MCP server on stdin/stdout so AI agents can extract, search and query APKs. Tools: extract, summary, find, class, callers, callees, sql, source, insights, xref, reach, smali, icon, findings, endpoints.
  diff        Compare two extracted versions: app facts, permissions, components, deep links, SDKs, libraries, hosts, URLs, native code, packages, classes, strings and resources.
  findings    Show review findings (debuggable, cleartext, exported components, WebView bridges, weak crypto, trust-all TLS, embedded secrets, …) with evidence. They are static observations to check, not proven vulnerabilities.
  xref        Where is a class or field used: instantiations, casts, instanceof, const-class, calls into its methods, field reads and writes.
  reach       Find call paths from an entry point (e.g. an exported activity) to target methods, following virtual and interface dispatch into subclasses. Static approximation: reflection, framework callbacks and native code are not followed.
  smali       Print smali (bytecode assembly) for one class or method. Works where decompiling fails; # 0x… offsets match the code files.
  icon        Find the app icon: every file behind android:icon (or --round) per density, adaptive icon layers, pixel sizes, and the best file to use. -o saves it.
  components  List activities, aliases, services, receivers and providers with verdicts: launcher, app-link, deep-link, hidden-entry, task-hijack, lock-screen, exported-by-default, guarded, disabled.
  component   Explain one component: verdicts with reasons, activity attributes, intent filters in plain words, deep links, aliases and ready-to-run adb commands.

docs.title: Exit codes and errors
docs.text:
Code Meaning Examples 0 Success 1 Usage error Unknown command or option, missing argument 2 Input error File not found, not a zip, no AndroidManifest.xml, undecodable manifest, bad SQL, unknown class or method 3 Output error Output folder not empty without --force, not writable 4 Internal error A bug; please report it with the APK's sha256 5 Findings gate findings --fail-on <severity> found at least one finding at or above that severity

Errors are printed to stderr with a hint when there is an obvious fix:

$ sextant extract app.apk -o busy/
Error: output directory busy is not empty
hint: pass --force to overwrite Sextant's files in it

--force only replaces Sextant's own files in the folder; nothing else is touched or deleted.

For an internal error, set SEXTANT_DEBUG=1 to print the stack trace:

SEXTANT_DEBUG=1 sextant extract app.apk -o out/

docs.title: Hostile and broken input
docs.text: Sextant never executes anything from an APK and never writes outside the output folder. Inflation is capped (manifest 32 MB, resources.arsc 512 MB, each dex 256 MB, each native library 256 MB) as a zip-bomb guard. Malformed parts become entries in meta.json → warnings instead of crashes: a dex that can't be read, methods with unreadable bytecode, an undecodable resource table, an unsigned or invalid signature.

docs.title: Review findings
docs.text:
sextant findings (and insights/findings.jsonl) report static observations to review, not proven vulnerabilities. Each finding lists the evidence: a manifest entry, a method, a string or a resource. At most 25 evidence items are kept per finding; count is exact.

Severity Meaning high Usually a real problem in a release build; check first medium Worth checking; often fine with the right context low Common patterns that deserve a look in a focused review info Context, not a problem by itself

docs.title: Manifest
docs.text: ID Severity Fires when debuggable high android:debuggable="true" test-only medium android:testOnly="true" (debug/test build; only installable with adb install -t) cleartext medium android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" cleartext-default low Cleartext is allowed by default: targetSdk < 28, no network security config, attribute not set exported-provider medium An exported, enabled provider with no permission, readPermission or writePermission exported-provider-partial low An exported provider with only one of readPermission / writePermission (the other direction is open) exported-component low Exported, enabled activities/services/receivers without a permission (launcher activities excluded) uri-grants-any-path info An exported provider with grantUriPermissions="true" and no <grant-uri-permission> elements task-affinity info Activities with a taskAffinity other than the package, or allowTaskReparenting="true" shared-user-id low android:sharedUserId is set (deprecated; shares process and data with other apps) profileable-shell low <profileable android:shell="true"> allow-backup info android:allowBackup="true" legacy-storage info requestLegacyExternalStorage="true"

docs.title: Code
docs.text: ID Severity Fires when trust-all-certificates high An X509TrustManager.checkServerTrusted implementation has an empty body accept-all-hostnames medium A HostnameVerifier.verify implementation has at most two instructions (likely return true) webview-js-bridge medium WebView.addJavascriptInterface is called webview-file-access medium WebSettings.setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs is called dynamic-code medium DexClassLoader / InMemoryDexClassLoader is constructed weak-cipher low A method loads DES, RC4, Blowfish, an …/ECB/… transformation or bare "AES", and calls Cipher.getInstance weak-hash low A method loads MD5, MD2, MD4 or SHA-1 and calls MessageDigest.getInstance exec low Runtime.exec or ProcessBuilder.start is called seeded-random low SecureRandom.setSeed is called webview-javascript info WebSettings.setJavaScriptEnabled is called

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Found in code string constants and string resources. Values are masked (first 6 and last 4 characters).

ID Severity Pattern secret-private-key high A PEM private-key header followed by base64 key material (a bare header, as used by parsers, is ignored) secret-aws-key high AKIA + 16 characters secret-stripe-live high sk_live_… secret-slack-token high xox[baprs]-… secret-github-token high gh[pousr]_ + 36 characters jwt medium Three base64url segments starting with eyJ google-api-key info AIza… (Google keys in apps are usually public by design; check they are restricted)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
{"id":"weak-hash","severity":"low","title":"Weak hash algorithm",
 "detail":"MD5/SHA-1 are not collision resistant; fine for checksums, not for security decisions.",
 "evidence":[{"kind":"method","where":"Lde/…/DecodeActivity;->C(Ljava/lang/String;[B)V","value":"SHA-1"}],"count":3}

In the index: tables findings and finding_evidence, plus the finding search kind.

docs.title: SARIF and CI
docs.text:
sextant findings app/ --sarif > sextant.sarif        # SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning, GitLab, dashboards
sextant findings app/ --fail-on high                 # exit code 5 if there is any high finding
Sextant severity SARIF level GitHub security-severity high error 8.0 medium warning 5.0 low note 3.0 info note 1.0

Each evidence item becomes a location: AndroidManifest.xml for manifest evidence, resources.arsc for resources, and smali/<class path>.smali for code, with the component, method descriptor or resource name as the logical location. See Security review → In CI for a complete GitHub Actions workflow.

docs.title: SQLite index schema
docs.text:
index.sqlite holds everything in the output folder, normalized. Every method reference (defined in the APK or external) has one row in methods; edges point at integer ids, and the views call_edges, string_uses and search_items give the readable, descriptor-based form. JSON arrays are stored as TEXT; use SQLite's json_each to expand them. Query it with sextant sql <dir> "…" (read-only) or any SQLite tool.

Schema version: 6 (stored in meta as index_schema_version).

CREATE TABLE meta (
  key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE permissions (
  name             TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind             TEXT NOT NULL,   -- uses-permission | uses-permission-sdk-23 | implied | declared
  max_sdk          INTEGER,
  dangerous        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  protection_level TEXT,
  custom           INTEGER NOT NULL,
  implied_by       TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE components (
  type            TEXT NOT NULL,    -- activity | activity-alias | service | receiver | provider
  name            TEXT NOT NULL,
  exported        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  exported_source TEXT NOT NULL,    -- explicit | default
  enabled         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  permission      TEXT,
  process         TEXT,
  launcher        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  target_activity TEXT,
  authorities     TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON array
  intent_filters  TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON array, same shape as components.jsonl
  read_permission         TEXT,     -- providers
  write_permission        TEXT,     -- providers
  grant_uri_permissions   INTEGER,  -- providers; NULL = not set
  path_permissions        TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON array of <path-permission>
  launch_mode             TEXT,     -- activities
  task_affinity           TEXT,     -- activities
  foreground_service_type TEXT,     -- services
  isolated_process        INTEGER,
  direct_boot_aware       INTEGER,
  label                   TEXT,
  tags                    TEXT NOT NULL, -- JSON array of verdicts: launcher, app-link, deep-link, hidden-entry, task-hijack, …
  activity                TEXT      -- activities: JSON object of the other <activity> attributes that are set
);

-- uses-feature / uses-library / uses-native-library
CREATE TABLE features (
  kind     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- feature | library | native-library
  name     TEXT NOT NULL,
  required INTEGER,                 -- NULL = not set (defaults to required)
  version  TEXT
);

-- meta-data and property on the application (scope = 'application') or a component (scope = class name)
CREATE TABLE metadata (
  scope    TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- meta-data | property
  name     TEXT NOT NULL,
  value    TEXT,
  resource TEXT
);

-- <queries>: package visibility (Android 11+)
CREATE TABLE queries (
  kind       TEXT NOT NULL,         -- package | intent | provider
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  actions    TEXT NOT NULL,         -- JSON array
  categories TEXT NOT NULL,         -- JSON array
  data       TEXT NOT NULL          -- JSON array
);

CREATE TABLE deep_links (
  component TEXT NOT NULL,
  url       TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE classes (
  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  descriptor   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, -- Lcom/app/Foo;
  name         TEXT NOT NULL,        -- com.app.Foo
  package      TEXT NOT NULL,
  superclass   TEXT,
  interfaces   TEXT NOT NULL,        -- JSON array of descriptors
  access       TEXT NOT NULL,        -- space separated
  source_file  TEXT,
  dex          TEXT NOT NULL,
  kotlin       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  annotations  TEXT NOT NULL,        -- JSON array of descriptors
  method_count INTEGER NOT NULL,
  field_count  INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- Every method reference. defined = 1 for methods with a definition in the APK; external ones have NULL details.
CREATE TABLE methods (
  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  descriptor   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, -- Lcom/app/Foo;->bar(I)V
  class        TEXT NOT NULL,        -- Lcom/app/Foo;
  name         TEXT NOT NULL,
  defined      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  params       TEXT,                 -- JSON array of type descriptors
  return_type  TEXT,
  access       TEXT,
  has_code     INTEGER,
  instructions INTEGER,
  registers    INTEGER,
  calls_out    INTEGER,
  string_loads INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE fields (
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  descriptor    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, -- Lcom/app/Foo;->count:I
  class         TEXT NOT NULL,
  name          TEXT NOT NULL,
  type          TEXT NOT NULL,
  access        TEXT NOT NULL,
  initial_value TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE calls (
  caller  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES methods(id),
  callee  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES methods(id),
  kind    TEXT NOT NULL,             -- virtual | static | direct | super | interface | polymorphic
  count   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  offsets TEXT NOT NULL              -- JSON array, 16-bit code units, max 32
);

CREATE TABLE strings (
  id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
);

CREATE TABLE string_refs (
  string  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES strings(id),
  method  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES methods(id),
  count   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  offsets TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- Field reads/writes and type uses (new, const-class, check-cast, instance-of, arrays) per method.
CREATE TABLE field_refs (
  method  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES methods(id),
  field   TEXT NOT NULL,             -- Lcom/app/Foo;->count:I
  kind    TEXT NOT NULL,             -- read | write
  count   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  offsets TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE type_refs (
  method  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES methods(id),
  type    TEXT NOT NULL,             -- Lcom/app/Foo;
  kind    TEXT NOT NULL,             -- new | class | cast | instanceof | array
  count   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  offsets TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW call_edges AS
  SELECT a.descriptor AS caller, b.descriptor AS callee, c.kind, c.count, c.offsets
  FROM calls c JOIN methods a ON a.id = c.caller JOIN methods b ON b.id = c.callee;

CREATE VIEW string_uses AS
  SELECT s.value, m.descriptor AS method, r.count, r.offsets
  FROM string_refs r JOIN strings s ON s.id = r.string JOIN methods m ON m.id = r.method;

-- Version 5 insights.
CREATE TABLE libraries (
  "group"  TEXT NOT NULL,
  artifact TEXT NOT NULL,
  version  TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE frameworks (
  name     TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence TEXT NOT NULL             -- JSON array
);

CREATE TABLE sdks (
  name     TEXT NOT NULL,
  category TEXT NOT NULL,
  classes  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  packages TEXT NOT NULL,            -- JSON array
  manifest TEXT NOT NULL             -- JSON array
);

CREATE TABLE endpoints (
  id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  url    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  scheme TEXT NOT NULL,
  host   TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE endpoint_sources (
  endpoint INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES endpoints(id),
  kind     TEXT NOT NULL,            -- code | resource | deep_link | manifest | asset | native
  location TEXT NOT NULL             -- method descriptor, @string/name or component
);

CREATE TABLE resources (
  type  TEXT NOT NULL,               -- string | bool | integer | color | dimen
  name  TEXT NOT NULL,
  value TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE native_libraries (
  path             TEXT NOT NULL,
  abi              TEXT NOT NULL,
  name             TEXT NOT NULL,
  size_bytes       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sha256           TEXT NOT NULL,
  elf_class        TEXT,
  exported_symbols INTEGER NOT NULL,
  jni_methods      INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE native_symbols (
  library    TEXT NOT NULL,
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  jni_class  TEXT,
  jni_method TEXT
);

-- Launcher icon files: role is icon | round_icon, or <role>.background/.foreground/.monochrome for adaptive layers.
CREATE TABLE icons (
  role       TEXT NOT NULL,
  resource   TEXT NOT NULL,          -- @mipmap/ic_launcher
  path       TEXT NOT NULL,          -- file inside the APK
  config     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- xxxhdpi-v4, anydpi-v26, …
  density    INTEGER,                -- dpi; NULL for anydpi/nodpi
  format     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- png | webp | jpg | gif | xml
  width      INTEGER,
  height     INTEGER,
  size_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
  best       INTEGER NOT NULL        -- 1 for the file Sextant picks to show
);

-- Review findings (static observations to check, not proven vulnerabilities).
CREATE TABLE findings (
  id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  severity TEXT NOT NULL,            -- high | medium | low | info
  title    TEXT NOT NULL,
  detail   TEXT NOT NULL,
  count    INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE finding_evidence (
  finding  TEXT NOT NULL,            -- findings.id
  kind     TEXT NOT NULL,            -- manifest | method | class | string | resource
  location TEXT NOT NULL,
  value    TEXT
);

-- Substring search (trigram: any 3+ character fragment matches). Contentless to save space:
-- rowid = (source id << 4) | kind; kinds: 1 class, 2 method, 3 field, 4 string, 5 component, 6 permission,
-- 7 deep_link, 8 resource, 9 endpoint, 10 sdk, 11 library, 12 native_symbol, 13 finding.
-- Indexed text: class full name; method and field "SimpleClass.name" (field + " = value"); first 1000 chars of strings.
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE search USING fts5(text, content = '', tokenize = 'trigram');

-- What each search rowid points at, for SQL users:
--   SELECT i.kind, i.ref, i.text FROM search JOIN search_items i ON i.search_rowid = search.rowid WHERE search MATCH 'Cipher'
CREATE VIEW search_items AS
  SELECT id * 16 + 1 AS search_rowid, 'class' AS kind, descriptor AS ref, name AS text FROM classes
  UNION ALL SELECT id * 16 + 2, 'method', descriptor, descriptor FROM methods
  UNION ALL SELECT id * 16 + 3, 'field', descriptor, descriptor || coalesce(' = ' || initial_value, '') FROM fields
  UNION ALL SELECT id * 16 + 4, 'string', id, value FROM strings
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 5, 'component', name, type || ' ' || name FROM components
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 6, 'permission', name, name FROM permissions
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 7, 'deep_link', component, url FROM deep_links
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 8, 'resource', '@' || type || '/' || name, name || ' = ' || value FROM resources
  UNION ALL SELECT id * 16 + 9, 'endpoint', url, url FROM endpoints
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 10, 'sdk', name, name || ' (' || category || ')' FROM sdks
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 11, 'library', "group" || ':' || artifact, "group" || ':' || artifact || ':' || version FROM libraries
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 12, 'native_symbol', library, name FROM native_symbols
  UNION ALL SELECT rowid * 16 + 13, 'finding', id, severity || ' ' || title FROM findings;

Indexes created after loading:

CREATE INDEX methods_class ON methods(class);
CREATE INDEX methods_name ON methods(name);
CREATE INDEX fields_class ON fields(class);
CREATE INDEX classes_name ON classes(name);
CREATE INDEX classes_super ON classes(superclass);
CREATE INDEX calls_caller ON calls(caller);
CREATE INDEX calls_callee ON calls(callee);
CREATE INDEX string_refs_string ON string_refs(string);
CREATE INDEX string_refs_method ON string_refs(method);
CREATE INDEX components_name ON components(name);
CREATE INDEX permissions_name ON permissions(name);
CREATE INDEX endpoints_host ON endpoints(host);
CREATE INDEX field_refs_field ON field_refs(field);
CREATE INDEX field_refs_method ON field_refs(method);
CREATE INDEX type_refs_type ON type_refs(type);
CREATE INDEX endpoint_sources_endpoint ON endpoint_sources(endpoint);
CREATE INDEX native_symbols_jni_class ON native_symbols(jni_class);

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
sextant extract app.apk -o app/ writes this folder. Every file is UTF-8 with \n line endings. Keys are snake_case in a fixed order, and lists are sorted, so the same APK always gives byte-identical files.

app/
  summary.md          ← read this first (short, written for people and agents)
  meta.json           ← identity, SDKs, application flags, signing, layout, code + insight counts, icons, warnings
  manifest.json       ← the full decoded AndroidManifest.xml as a tree
  permissions.jsonl   ← one permission per line
  components.jsonl    ← one component per line (activities, aliases, services, receivers, providers)
  features.jsonl      ← uses-feature / uses-library / uses-native-library
  metadata.jsonl      ← meta-data and property (application and components)
  queries.jsonl       ← <queries>: packages, intents, providers the app can see
  code/
    classes.jsonl     ← one class per line
    methods.jsonl     ← one method per line
    fields.jsonl      ← one field per line, with constant initial values
    calls.jsonl       ← caller → callee edges with bytecode offsets
    strings.jsonl     ← string constants and the methods that load them
    field_refs.jsonl  ← field reads/writes per method
    type_refs.jsonl   ← new / const-class / check-cast / instance-of / arrays per method
  insights/
    frameworks.jsonl  ← Flutter, React Native, .NET MAUI, Unity, … with evidence
    sdks.jsonl        ← known SDKs by category, with class and manifest evidence
    libraries.jsonl   ← exact Maven coordinates + versions
    endpoints.jsonl   ← every URL and where it was found
    findings.jsonl    ← review points with evidence
  resources/
    values.jsonl      ← default strings, bools, integers, colors, dimens
  native/
    libraries.jsonl   ← .so files per ABI: size, sha256, exported symbols, JNI methods
    symbols.jsonl     ← exported functions; JNI symbols mapped to Java
  index.sqlite        ← all of the above, normalized, with full-text search

--no-code skips code/ (and code-based insights); --no-index skips index.sqlite.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• null means absent. A manifest attribute that isn't set is null, never a guessed default. Values Sextant derives say so (exported_source, implied_by).
  • IDs are smali descriptors: Lcom/a/B; (class), Lcom/a/B;->m(I)V (method), Lcom/a/B;->f:I (field).
  • Offsets in code/*.jsonl are 16-bit code units (decimal), the same unit dexdump and smali (#@hex) use. At most 32 are kept per record; count is always exact.
  • Strings with unpaired UTF-16 surrogates (possible in DEX) are written as \uXXXX escapes, so the files stay valid UTF-8.
  • schema_version in meta.json changes only when the shape of the files changes, independently of the tool version (currently 7).

  • exported is the effective value: an explicit android:exported wins; otherwise components with an intent filter are exported, and providers are exported only for apps whose minSdk or targetSdk is 16 or lower. exported_source says which (explicit or default).
  • launcher is true for activities with MAIN + LAUNCHER.
  • Intent filter data also carries ssp, ssp_prefix, ssp_pattern, path_suffix, path_advanced_pattern, port and mime_type.
